20261118-chemistry-e4.title: Where dis water drops come from
20261118-chemistry-e4.topic: Where dis water drops come from
20261118-chemistry-e4.goal: Apply the principles of Where dis water drops come from to solve the reasoning problem.
20261118-chemistry-e4.material: Dem take cold drink can comot from fridge just now and put am for table for small time, and small water drops form for di surface of di can. Where dis water drops come from?
20261118-chemistry-e4.thinking.0: Where dis water drops come from
20261118-chemistry-e4.s.s1.prompt: Dem take cold drink can comot from fridge just now and put am for table for small time, and small water drops form for di surface of di can. Where dis water drops come from?
20261118-chemistry-e4.s.s1.explain: Na 'condensation (liquefaction)' be dis: di water vapor wey dey gas state inside air meet di cold can surface, lose heat, and turn liquid water drops.
20261118-chemistry-e4.s.s1.hint.0: Water vapor wey you no fit see dey always float inside air.
20261118-chemistry-e4.s.s1.hint.1: Wen water vapor meet cold surface e cool down and turn liquid water drops (condensation).
20261118-chemistry-e4.s.s1.o.o0: Water vapor (gas) wey dey inside air touch di cold can and condense into liquid water
20261118-chemistry-e4.s.s1.o.o1: Di drink leak comot through di aluminium wall of di can

20261122-chemistry-e4-1.material: [Advanced change of state] Dem put water inside beaker and heat am until e start to boil hard. Even if dem increase di flame and continue to heat am, di thermometer reading no go up pass 100℃ anymore. Why?
20261122-chemistry-e4-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced change of state] Dem put water inside beaker and heat am until e start to boil hard. Even if dem increase di flame and continue to heat am, di thermometer reading no go up pass 100℃ anymore. Why?
20261122-chemistry-e4-1.s.s1.explain: While pure liquid dey boil, all di heat energy wey dem add dey use to break di attraction between molecules and change to gas state (heat of vaporization), so di temperature dey remain constant until all di water don turn vapor.
20261122-chemistry-e4-1.s.s1.hint.0: Di temperature of matter dey remain constant while di state dey change.
20261122-chemistry-e4-1.s.s1.hint.1: Dem dey call dis 'latent heat (heat of vaporization)'.
20261122-chemistry-e4-1.s.s1.o.o0: Because di heat energy wey dem supply no dey raise di water temperature but dem use all of am for di change of state wey water dey turn vapor (heat of vaporization)
20261122-chemistry-e4-1.s.s1.o.o1: Because thermometer dey spoil for above 100 degrees
20261122-chemistry-e4-1.s.s1.o.o2: Because water no fit absorb heat again
20261122-chemistry-e4-1.s.s1.o.o3: Because di water vapor dey cool di thermometer
